subject: general
question: Find the value of (3)/(sin ^ 2A secA) x 3sqrt{tan ^ 2A - Sin ^ 2A}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **A = 45°** to simplify the **trigonometric expression**.

sin²A = 1/2, secA = √2, tan²A = 1.

Expression = [3 ÷ (1/2 × √2)] × 3√(1 − 1/2) = [3 × 2 / √2] × 3√(1/2) = 3√2 × 3/√2 = 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Expr = (3 / (sin²A secA)) × 3√(tan²A − sin²A)

**Formula Used:** tan²A − sin²A = tan²A sin²A; secA = 1/cosA

⇒ Simplify the square root term: √(tan²A − sin²A) = √((sin²A/cos²A) − sin²A)

⇒ √(sin²A(1/cos²A − 1)) = √(sin²A(sec²A − 1)) = √(sin²A tan²A) = sinA tanA

⇒ Substitute back into the expression: (3 / (sin²A × (1/cosA))) × 3(sinA tanA)

⇒ (3 cosA / sin²A) × 3 sinA × (sinA / cosA)

⇒ (9 × cosA × sin²A) / (sin²A × cosA) = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Product-Difference Identity

For any angle A, **tan²A − sin²A = tan²A × sin²A** and similarly **cot²A − cos²A = cot²A × cos²A**.

Reciprocal Relations

**secA = 1/cosA**, **cosecA = 1/sinA**, and **tanA = sinA/cosA**.

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental identities: **sin²A + cos²A = 1** and **1 + tan²A = sec²A**.</p
